transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-30
Start time: 16:00 UTC (09:00 PT)
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Carlos Rios (HelioPath Head of ML), Priya Desai (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (CTO)

Summary:
HelioPath is evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a latency-sensitive inference pipeline (customer search/responses). Primary goals: p95 latency < 250ms for streaming tokens in baseline paths, support bursts to 1.2k concurrent streams, steady-state token/sec targets ~ 20k tokens/sec across cluster. Security constraints (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS) push them toward Dedicated/Private but cost tradeoffs are a concern. Agreement to run a Redwood-hosted benchmark (48-72h) and share detailed traffic model and prompts.

Topics:
- p95 targets and how we measure
- concurrency and multiplexing considerations
- streaming vs non-streaming token/sec benchmarking
- hosted fallback and model variants
- security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? Ich I'll - uh - I'm Maya (AE) and Jordan (SE) is with me.
[00:16] Jordan (Redwood): hi all, jordan here, will be driving perf and the bench stuff, happy to dig into KV cache and batching.
[00:28] Carlos (HelioPath): Carlos here, head of ML. We run a real-time assistant inside our platform, need low p95 latency for streaming completions, and we have bursts from scheduled events.
[00:42] Priya (HelioPath): Priya, platform eng, I manage infra and networking, curious about VPC and private nats and how Redwood Dedicated would sit in our VPC.
[00:56] Liam (HelioPath): Liam, CTO. My main question is predictability — costs and tail latency.
[01:10] Maya: great. High level — Redwood offers Hosted API for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private for VPC/on-prem. Today is about mapping your p95 and concurrency targets to those modes.
[01:29] Carlos: we have a p95 target of around 200-250ms for token streaming for the main assist flow, that includes network time to our edge and Redwood processing. Our median is fine, it's the tail that kills UX.
[01:44] Jordan: ok, 200-250ms p95 streaming — couple quick qualifiers: what model family are you planning to serve? Larger models have higher per-token compute.
[01:59] Carlos: currently using an open Llama-variant (we call it LL-v2-13b) quantized to int8 on our infra, but we are open to model variants. We'll want the platform to support quantized paths and fallback to fp16 if needed.
[02:15] Maya: note — we have Redwood-verified profiles for similar models. For streaming p95 we usually look at end-to-end measured at the token emission boundary; we account for KV cache warmup.
[02:30] Priya: security questions up front: do you have SOC 2 Type II? SAML SSO? KMS integration for customer keys?
[02:42] Maya: yes on SOC2, SSO via SAML/Okta supported, and KMS integration — we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations in Private mode. We'll send the security pack link after the call. (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-kms)
[02:58] Liam: if we do Dedicated, how isolated is network and data? We need logs for auditing and retention.
[03:10] Jordan: Dedicated gives isolated compute pools and per-tenant token logs, you can configure retention. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and networking so logs and keys never leave your VPC.
[03:25] Carlos: ok. On load: we see steady-state ~6-8k tokens/sec, with scheduled bursts up to ~22k tokens/sec for 15-30 minutes, and peak concurrency ~1.2k active streams. How would Redwood plan capacity for that?
[03:42] Jordan: rough rule — steady-state handled by reserved GPU pools sized with buffer. For bursts we can do autoscaling + burst capacity; Dedicated can be configured with burst credits. For streaming p95 the kernel selection and batching strategy matter a lot. We need token length distribution and prompt sizes to give a more precise plan.
[03:59] Priya: we also have a strict SLA requirement the app must not exceed 500ms p95 even under burst if possible — otherwise degrade gracefully with a lighter model. Can Redwood do automatic fallback?
[04:15] Maya: yes, we support runtime routing policies: prefer the target model, fallback to smaller variant or quantized variant automatically. You can set per-route latency SLOs and fallback rules.
[04:30] Carlos: curious bout measurement: do you instrument p95 at the server side or just client? We need to have one source of truth for SLA.
[04:42] Jordan: we provide both. Redwood Console surfaces token-level latency breakdowns (network, queuing, kernel time). For benchmarking we suggest running against the Redwood hosted test endpoint and also capturing client-side latencies.
[04:58] Liam: cost — Dedicated reserved is more $$ up front but predictable. Any ballpark numbers for 13B-like model serving at our scale?
[05:10] Maya: I'll share the capacity/pricing matrix — ballpark depends a lot on sequence length and quantization. We can run a 48-72 hour benchmark to get real numbers.
[05:22] Priya: we need the benchmark harness to run in our VPC if we do Private. If hosted, we want representative traffic to avoid surprises.
[05:34] Jordan: agreed. For hosted benchmark we spin up a test app and run a 72h p95 streaming run with your prompt set — we'll provide the harness (k6-based) and sample Redwood config. For Private we'll help with on-prem agent or VPC peering.
[05:52] Carlos: one of our pain points today: cold starts cause the p95 to spike; how does Redwood handle cold KV warms?
[06:03] Jordan: we have prefix cache and pre-warming approaches; for Dedicated you can reserve warmed workers for critical routes to avoid cold starts, and the runtime supports continuous batching to smooth tails.
[06:17] Carlos: hm. Also interested in quantization impact on tail latency vs accuracy.
[06:26] Jordan: quantization reduces memory and can improve per-token throughput but kernel characteristics differ; we'll recommend profiles per model. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization levels per workload.
[06:40] Liam: on compliance, we'd need access logs and an audit trail for three years — is that supported?
[06:50] Maya: yes, audit log retention is configurable as an add-on; Private deployments make it easier to meet long retention and residency constraints.
[07:02] Priya: networking — can Dedicated sit behind our NAT and route egress through our proxy?
[07:10] Jordan: Dedicated can be configured with customer-managed NAT and VPC peering depending on cloud. In Private install it's fully within your network.
[07:22] Carlos: ok, let's map out the concrete bench plan. We want p95 measured at our edge, and also server-side breakdown. We want to push to 1.2k concurrency, steady 20k tokens/sec for 30 min to see queuing behavior.
[07:40] Jordan: good. For that we'll suggest running a mix: 60% mid-length (average 40 tokens), 30% short (10 tokens), 10% long (200+ tokens) to match your mix. We'll supply the k6 script and example config.
[07:58] Liam: do you support streaming HTTP/2 and websockets? Our clients are web and mobile.
[08:07] Maya: yes, streaming with chunked responses and websocket-based streaming are both supported; we'll show examples in the dev quickstart. (link: https://redwood.example.com/dev/streaming)
[08:21] Carlos: any gotchas around load testing that have bitten folks?
[08:27] Jordan: two common things: (1) synthetic load that doesn't mirror token length distribution gives optimistic throughput; (2) hitting autoscale limits without buffer causes transient queues — so plan for reserved buffer or burst credits.
[08:42] Carlos: ok noted.
[08:46] Priya: if we go Private, how invasive is the on-prem package? We are ISO27001 and have air-gapped staging environments.
[08:55] Maya: the Private package can be air-gapped; we ship a deployable control plane image plus an agent. For air-gapped installs we do a security checklist and run the install with your infra team.
[09:08] Liam: timeline — we're aiming for a Q3 pilot, production Q4, assuming security checks out. That is about 12 weeks from demo to pilot.
[09:21] Maya: that timeline is reasonable. Pilot usually involves a dedicated pool for your load and the 72h bench as acceptance.
[09:32] Carlos: what about SLOs during pilot — can Redwood set automated fallbacks to keep UX under 500ms p95?
[09:41] Jordan: yes, route policies can move traffic to smaller model variants or cached responses; we can set canary rules and automatic rollback.
[09:51] Priya: curious about tracing and observability—do you emit traces we can hook into Jaeger/Zipkin?
[09:58] Jordan: we expose spans and traces which can be exported; Redwood Console will show per-route traces and you can integrate with your existing observability.
[10:10] Carlos: ok let's talk about measurement specifics — how do you measure p95 for streaming where tokens arrive over time?
[10:19] Jordan: good q. For streaming we measure the time to first token and then per-token emission times; p95 is measured on the first meaningful token for UX and also on final token completion depending on the route. We'll provide both.
[10:36] Liam: if we need lower latency than Hosted can provide, is Dedicated typically enough?
[10:43] Jordan: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor and gives control over instance types and kernel choices so yes, for strict p95 it's often sufficient. Private gives the most control but higher ops burden.
[10:55] Maya: any other blockers from your side?
[11:00] Carlos: one more — encryption at rest and in-flight, we need KMS where keys never leave our account.
[11:07] Maya: supported in Private and Dedicated for customer-managed keys — we'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[11:15] Priya: can you also provide an example of autoscale policy that keeps latencies below threshold but doesn't overprovision cost?
[11:24] Jordan: yes, we have policy templates — e.g., p95-based scale-up with warmup buffer and burst credits. We'll share the template.
[11:36] Liam: pricing ask again — can you give a delta between Hosted per-token and Dedicated reserved for our estimated volumes?
[11:45] Maya: I'll send the spreadsheet; we should run the bench to produce actual numbers.
[11:52] Carlos: agreed. Let's agree next steps.
[12:00] Maya: recap: Redwood will share pricing/capacity sheet, security pack, bench harness and a proposed Redwood config. HelioPath will share prompt set and traffic distribution. We'll run a 48-72h hosted benchmark first, then evaluate Dedicated/Private options.
[12:18] Priya: timeline to get those docs over? Can we see pricing by Tuesday?
[12:24] Maya: yes, Tuesday (2025-06-02) for pricing; Jordan will send bench materials by Thursday (2025-06-04).
[12:35] Carlos: sounds good. Anything else?
[12:38] Liam: no, thanks everyone.
[12:42] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the bench plan.

End of transcript.
